host: Apple M4 Pro, 48 GiB, macOS 26.5.2, Swift 6.3.3
why_not_pricing: 128-token window, one leg per arm, no counterbalancing, candidate-generated reference rows. The advisor's standing rule is that --local-submit is a correctness and gate check only.

void_run.verdict: VOID - measured the base kernel, not the candidate
void_run.root_cause: benchmark-qwen-mtp.sh extracts benchmark.sh's metallib_rebuild_required() but not its sibling swift_build_required(), so it refreshed mlx.metallib from candidate source and left .build-worker/release/mlxfast-runtime-worker on base source. quantized has an mlx-generated twin, so the runtime-effective source is the JIT string inside the worker binary - the half that was not refreshed.

incidental_base_vs_candidate_pair.note: The void run is a base-arm 128-token leg and the valid run is a candidate-arm 128-token leg, so the pair looks like a comparison. It is not one.
incidental_base_vs_candidate_pair.reading: Both legs moved by the same ~0.29 % in the same direction and the ratio is flat. The candidate cannot change the serial depth-0 leg, because M=1 falls through to qmv_fast_impl and never reaches the crossrow path. A serial move of the same size as the MTP move is therefore session drift, not signal. n=1 per arm, no counterbalancing, ~20 minutes apart, different thermal histories, and 56.2 % of a 128-token leg is prefill. This pair neither supports nor contradicts the rung 3 headline and is recorded only so nobody mistakes it for evidence later.

worker_text_sha256_retraction_reconfirme.note: This worker demonstrably embeds <T, 6, 6, true>, yet its __TEXT,__text digest equals the digest a base-arm build produced during rung 2. Second independent confirmation that the section digest tracks link layout, not kernel content, and is not a build witness.
